plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Sell high-beta names METU, MUU, PLTU as they are below stops.
Trim QQQI to 20% to cure the concentration mandate breach.
Add to SPY, increasing broad index exposure for stability.
This plan aims for capital preservation and lower drawdown.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and high-beta names. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns.

plan: Trim SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU to reduce overall leverage and high-beta exposure.
Trim QQQI to 20% to address the concentration mandate breach.
Buy ALB, a strong scanner long setup, to add quality growth.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF presence.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets ~2.5%/month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a quality new name. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Add to SOXL, SPAL, METU, MUU, PLTU to increase leveraged and high-beta exposure.
Buy ALB and TXN, both strong scanner long setups, to add new growth.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
Strict stop discipline is crucial due to amplified risk and daily decay.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration, which amplifies both potential upside and drawdown. Be aware of leveraged ETF decay and the potential for rapid losses if stops are not strictly adhered to.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Sell high-beta single names (METU, MUU, PLTU, CRWD, SNOW) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, increasing exposure to income-generating ETFs.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It significantly reduces growth-oriented and high-beta holdings. While aiming for reliable distributions, NAV can still fall in a selloff, and distributions are variable.
